passages.heading: CM’s view of Ewa
passages.source: CM’s view of Ewa: Largely built out, Hoakalei, Gentry finished, new development in Hoopili. Ewa developed rapidly, 2013 plan has largely been built upon. Main planning challenges: traffic and safety, expanding and maintaining park and recreation, dealing with cesspool issues.

passages.heading: Resiliency
passages.source: Right now if a disaster happens, no one knows where to go, no facility. CM is Very interested in a resiliency hub concept. Reference to his prior experience in Kaʻū (Big Island), where a rec center acted as a hub during earthquakes, tsunamis. He suggested to use an existing or upgraded rec center (e.g., Mahiko or similar) as a hardened resiliency hub, with supplies and backup power.

passages.heading: Cess Pool
passages.source: ENV manages cesspool conversion district, there are 932 homes with cess pool in Ewa beach. City will pay connection to lateral into the main sewer line. After system is active, property owners have 30 days to connect. After connection, homeowners begin paying a sewer bill. Some homeowners currently pay nothing for sewer and resist this plan because they don’t want a new bill. Not sure how much the monthly bill will be. There is the CARE? program that help needy family reduce the bill.

passages.heading: Housing, jobs, and “Second City” role
passages.source:
New film facility in UH is in development process.
Many people still drive in town to work live in Ewa, adding to traffic. Councilmember hopes for more jobs in Kapolei / Ewa (Second City) so people can live and work in the region.
Many residents are local families getting their first home. Demographic has shifted from more rural / low-income perception to growing middle-class base. Emphasizes that Ewa community is strong: sports as central identity local teams and schools performing well.
Shoreline development: Oneula / Hoakalei New luxury housing going up. This area historically had significant homeless presence. Luxury homeowners will pressure for more enforcement and changes at the park and shoreline.
